subject: Capacity sizing & procurement conduit for Q4 Dedicated Fleet
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-08-09T09:12:00Z
Subject: Dedicated fleet sizing + lead time constraints for Q4

Hi Vanessa,

We're getting internal buy-in to move forward with a Dedicated deployment for our inference workloads, contingent on hitting a Q4 onramp. Before we lock a commitment window, procurement needs a realistic view of
- minimum GPU pool size you recommend for our initial phase (P99 latency SLO, 1.5x peak concurrency headroom),
- expected hardware procurement lead times (OEM) vs cloud-reserved alternatives, and
- any recommended phased approach so we can start with hybrid (some cloud capacity) while hardware ships.

Attached is a short RFP sketch with our model mix and expected token volumes. Can Redwood provide a short conduit plan (timeline + vendor coordination approach) we can include in the procurement packet?

Also flag any long-lead items (custom PCIe racks, firmware stacks, or compliance checks) we should pre-clear.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Platform, AcmeAI
Priya Shah
[attachment: Acme_RFP_requirements_v1.pdf]
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-09T11:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated fleet sizing + lead time constraints for Q4

Hi Priya — thanks for the RFP sketch. High level answer up front: we can meet a Q4 onramp with a staged plan that mixes reserved cloud capacity for the first 8–12 weeks and a staggered OEM hardware ingress to reach steady-state by week 12–16, depending on SKU availability.

Key recommendations (short):
- Sizing: Recommend starting with ~80 A100-equivalent devices for the first production tranche (approx. 400k tokens/min sustained with your model mix). This gives 1.5x headroom for peak loads and enables usual autoscaling levers.
- Phasing: Phase 1 (weeks 0–8): 30–40 GPUs reserved in OmegaCloud (low friction, faster procurement). Phase 2 (weeks 8–16): staggered AtlasOEM deliveries to fill to 80+ devices.
- Lead times: OEM typical lead 12–16 weeks for standard racks; custom racks/firmware adds lead. Cloud reserved capacity available in 2–4 weeks for most regions but requires financial commit & contract turnaround.
- Long-lead items: custom rack buildouts, KMS/HSM integration window for Private deployments, and SOC2 evidence collection if they require on-prem proofs.

I'll loop procurement and our vendor contacts to get ETA & preliminary quotes. Ben / Karthik — can you ping AtlasOEM and OmegaCloud for firm ETAs, cost delta for expedited OEM fulfillment, and any minimum commit terms? I'll draft a mutual action plan and share a link for approvals.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

(Attachments: Acme_RFP_requirements_v1.pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marco Rossi <m.rossi@atlas-oem.it>, Lisa Huang <lisa.huang@omegacloud.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-10T07:22:00Z
Subject: Request: preliminary ETA & terms for DEAL-8421 sizing plan

Hi Marco, hi Lisa —

Following up from Vanessa / Acme's RFP. We're working to build a procurement conduit so Acme can sign a Dedicated commitment with a clear delivery cadence. Quick asks so we can finalize a mutual action plan:
1) ETA windows: provide earliest and typical ship dates for 30, 40 and 80-unit tranches (A100-equivalent SKU or closest match). If you have a commit ladder / tranche model, include that cadence.
2) Expedited options: cost and calendar impact for an expedite lane (partial expedite acceptable).
3) Contracting terms: minimum commit term for cloud reservations (Lisa), cancellation windows, and any ramp flexibility.
4) Attachments: please attach a short quote & lead-time matrix and a PO template if available.

We'd like a short reply by COB 2027-08-11 to keep the procurement packet moving. Attaching our PO template for convenience.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[attachment: PO_template_redwood.docx]
From: Marco Rossi <m.rossi@atlas-oem.it>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lisa Huang <lisa.huang@omegacloud.com>
Date: 2027-08-11T12:10:00Z
Subject: AtlasOEM initial quote & lead-time guidance for DEAL-8421

Ben / Vanessa / team,

Thanks for the solicit. Summary below and attached initial quote (Atlas-Quote-8421.pdf).

- SKUs & equivalence: We propose Atlas-80X (A100-equivalent class).
- Standard lead time: 12–16 weeks from PO for standard rack-build inventory in our EU / US fabs. Earliest available slot currently shows 14 weeks for a clean PO executed this month.
- Staged deliveries: We can split into two tranches (40 + 40) with the first tranche at 12 weeks and the second tranche at +3–4 weeks after the first shipment (subject to inventory).
- Expedited option: Fast lane at ~+25% cost for allocation & air freight; reduces the first-tranche lead time to ~8–10 weeks depending on customs clearances.
- Minimum order: 20 units per tranche for commit pricing; PO template accepted.
- Notes: Custom rack config or HSM pre-integration adds 2–3 weeks to build time; firmware sign-off may require a test unit exchange window.

Attachment: Atlas-Quote-8421.pdf

Happy to hop on a call with procurement to align timelines and clarify technical constraints.

Best,
Marco Rossi
Channel Sales, AtlasOEM
[attachment: Atlas-Quote-8421.pdf]
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-11T15:45:00Z
Subject: RE: Capacity sizing & procurement conduit for Q4 Dedicated Fleet — plan & next steps

Team, Priya — thank you. Quick summary & action items to include in Acme's procurement packet so there is a single source of truth: 

Plan summary:
- Phase A (weeks 0–8): Reserve 35 GPUs in OmegaCloud (Lisa to confirm earliest activation & commit terms). This provides immediate capacity for go-live and keeps latency SLOs while OEM slots are open.
- Phase B (weeks 8–16): AtlasOEM deliver staggered tranches to reach 80 GPUs steady-state. First tranche target: 40 units at 12 weeks from signed PO; second tranche +3–4 weeks dependent on inventory.

Action items (owners & deadlines):
- Lisa (OmegaCloud): send reservation terms and earliest activation date by EOD 2027-08-12. (cc Lisa)
- Marco (AtlasOEM): confirm final quote & expedite cost breakdown by EOD 2027-08-12 so Acme can decide commit ladder. (cc Marco)
- Neha / Procurement at Redwood: prepare a draft mutual action plan and PO insert language for a staged-delivery clause — draft due 2027-08-13.
- Acme (Priya): confirm desired steady-state GPU count (80) or alternative target, and internal approval timeline for signed PO.
- Vanessa / Ben: schedule 30-minute alignment call on 2027-08-13 to review final terms and sign-off path.

Risks & contingencies:
- If OEM lead exceeds the 16-week window, we recommend extending Phase A cloud reservations for an additional 4 weeks or expanding the cloud tranche to 50 GPUs temporarily.
- Expedite lane is available but increases unit cost materially and requires early deposit.

I'll circulate a one-page mutual action plan link for signatures once Marco and Lisa confirm. Priya — let's aim to have a procurement-ready packet for your CPO by 2027-08-14.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
